newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Motor stocks quiet despite 1st half sales data.
newsitem.headline: Motor stocks quiet despite 1st half sales data.

text.p: Shares of auto manufacturers and distributors remained quiet despite encouraging sales data for the first half of the year announced by a leading trade body, dealers said on Thursday.
The Malaysian Motor Traders Association (MMTA) announced that vehicle sales grew by 22.7 percent in the first half of the year over the corresponding 1996 period.
Analysts said the growth in numbers were in line with market expectations.
"It is pretty much in line with my expectations. Demand is still quiet strong. I think it is very very decent," said Chehan Perera, auto analyst at ABN-Amro.

Just before the lunch break, the stock of Malaysia's biggest car maker, Proton was down 10 cents, while its car distributor EON was up 10 cents. Their associate Diversified Resources was up two cents.
Nissan distributor Tan Chong was down six cents.
But, Oriental Holdings, whose sales of Honda cars in the first half grew by 38.3 percent, was up 30 cents.
Toyota distributor UMW Holdings and Mercedes assembler Cycle and Carriage Bintang were all unchanged.
